entries.subject: DAMIT 3102: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-3102.txt. Model 3102, version 2019-06-24, pole (101°, 71°), period 16.52178 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 87 ±6 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 89.38 ± 1.1 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 195 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Marciniak et al. (2019), A&A 625, A139
entries.finding: [Marciniak et al. (2019), A&A 625, A139](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.06056) — retained primary publication; see the body-specific selection and calibration above.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 3103, pole ['352', '83'], [Model 3103](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/3103) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 3103: pole (352°, 83°), 16.52179 h, version 2019-06-24, archive diameter 91 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: Shown size Display reference radius "43.5 km (size-calibrated model)" (marciniak-2019-slow-asteroids) differs from the Small Bodies Occultations V4.0 record 141, DAMIT model 3103 diameter 77 ± 2 km (volume-equivalent; DAMIT model 3103 fitted to 1 occultation); the shown value is kept.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.
